SUPPORTERS.name: Boehringer Ingelheim
SUPPORTERS.focus: Two engines — cardio-renal-metabolic (finerenone/GDMT, CKM) and progressive fibrosing lung disease (IPF, PPF, SARD-ILD) — plus a rare-derm bet in GPP (IL-36).
SUPPORTERS.cost: If BI-relevant education lags, fibrosing-ILD diagnostic delay persists and patients lose irreversible lung function before antifibrotics start; on the CKM side the cardiology–nephrology–primary-care 'who owns the patient' confusion keeps finerenone/SGLT2 underused. A grant deferred one quarter is a full congress cycle of clinicians not re-trained before the next guideline update.
SUPPORTERS.opp: Decera already runs cardio-renal-metabolic and HF/SGLT2 — so instead of repeating CKM, differentiate on the fibrosing-ILD side no competitor teaches as a cross-specialty referral problem: a rheumatology↔pulmonology SARD-ILD co-management program (who screens, when to refer, when to start antifibrotics). It pairs BI's IPF/PPF and immunology interests and is white space against single-specialty ILD sessions.

SUPPORTERS.name: Novartis
SUPPORTERS.focus: Complement and B-cell immunology across nephrology (IgAN — complement) and rheumatology (Sjögren's — B-cell depletion).
SUPPORTERS.cost: IgAN is the most crowded competitor topic in this dataset. If the Novartis complement narrative isn't reinforced in-window it is drowned out by APRIL/BAFF and endothelin messaging from Vertex, Travere and others — and share-of-voice lost in a launch window is nearly impossible to recover.
SUPPORTERS.opp: Everyone teaches IgAN 'mechanism of novel agents.' Decera's un-owned slot is a sequencing & treat-to-target program — how to layer complement, endothelin and APRIL agents against proteinuria thresholds over time — which no competitor activity addresses and which carries a payer/real-world-evidence angle Decera can own.

SUPPORTERS.name: Travere Therapeutics
SUPPORTERS.focus: Single-asset IgAN focus with an unusual tilt toward nursing and primary-care continuity rather than specialist mechanism.
SUPPORTERS.cost: Travere's edge is adherence and continuity, not mechanism. If that education stalls, the PCP→nephrologist handoff gap stays open and early proteinuria control — the window where their asset differentiates — is lost. IgAN treatment initiation is front-loaded, so timing is decisive.
SUPPORTERS.opp: Competitors aim IgAN at nephrologists; Travere already funds nurses and PCPs. Decera can build the first IgAN care-team pathway program (PCP screening → referral triggers → nurse-led adherence monitoring) — interprofessional CE that specialist-only decks don't touch.

SUPPORTERS.name: AstraZeneca
SUPPORTERS.focus: Enabling optimal guideline-directed therapy — hyperkalemia management so RAASi/GDMT isn't down-titrated, plus ATTRv amyloid polyneuropathy diagnosis.
SUPPORTERS.cost: The hyperkalemia story is really a GDMT-continuation story. If clinicians aren't taught to manage potassium instead of stopping RAASi/MRAs, patients stay under-treated for HF/CKD and the binder rationale never lands. ATTR delay means years of continued misdiagnosis.
SUPPORTERS.opp: Hyperkalemia is already covered by Medtelligence and Power-Pak. Decera's white space is folding it into its existing cardio-renal-metabolic program as a 'keep patients on GDMT' retention module tied to real HF outcomes, rather than a standalone potassium-binder talk.

SUPPORTERS.name: Johnson & Johnson / Janssen
SUPPORTERS.focus: Immunology breadth — IL-23 dermatology (psoriasis), FcRn neuromuscular (gMG), and IBD.
SUPPORTERS.cost: In gMG the field is shifting fast to FcRn and complement; if partial-responder management isn't taught now, clinicians default to old escalation patterns and newer agents are mis-sequenced. Derm IL-23 durability messaging is perishable as orals and biosimilars crowd in.
SUPPORTERS.opp: Decera runs PsA+obesity and HS — adjacent immuno-derm. The differentiated move is a cross-indication IL-23 / 'treat-to-target' program spanning psoriasis→PsA→IBD (same pathway, different organs), which competitors teach as siloed single-disease sessions.

SUPPORTERS.name: Eli Lilly
SUPPORTERS.focus: Type-2 inflammation in derm (atopic dermatitis) plus the obesity–GI intersection (IBD + obesity), riding the incretin franchise into inflammatory disease.
SUPPORTERS.cost: The IBD–obesity link is still emerging. If it isn't taught, clinicians miss obesity as a modifiable driver of IBD outcomes and the incretin-era opportunity — a moment time-boxed to the current GLP-1 wave.
SUPPORTERS.opp: CME Outfitters already did IBD+obesity for Lilly. Decera can leapfrog with an obesity-as-a-cross-cutting-driver series spanning IBD, PsA and cardiometabolic disease (all already in Decera's portfolio) — one metabolic thread through multiple therapeutic areas, which no competitor packages.

SUPPORTERS.name: Takeda
SUPPORTERS.focus: GI (IBD) plus rare pulmonary/hepatic alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency (AATD).
SUPPORTERS.cost: AATD is chronically underdiagnosed — years of delay, irreversible emphysema and liver disease. Every cycle without clinician education is measurable lost lung function and missed genetic testing.
SUPPORTERS.opp: Decera can own an AATD case-finding program targeting the primary-care/pulmonology screening gap (who to test, how to interpret), an area only lightly touched by ACHL — pairing Takeda's rare-disease and GI/hepatology interests.

SUPPORTERS.name: CSL Vifor
SUPPORTERS.focus: Nephrology franchise — hyperkalemia binders and IgAN.
SUPPORTERS.cost: Overlaps AstraZeneca's potassium story; if the nephrology-specific continuation message lags, MRAs/RAASi keep getting stopped in CKD and renal-anemia adjacencies go untaught.
SUPPORTERS.opp: Differentiate from the crowded hyperkalemia field with a nephrology 'protect the kidney, keep the GDMT' pathway bundling hyperkalemia, anemia and IgAN into one CKD-progression program — integrated rather than single-drug.

SUPPORTERS.name: Vertex Pharmaceuticals
SUPPORTERS.focus: Nephrology entry via the IgAN complement pathway.
SUPPORTERS.cost: A new nephrology entrant in the most saturated topic here; without early education its mechanism is lost against incumbents and launch-window share-of-voice is unrecoverable.
SUPPORTERS.opp: Same un-owned slot as Novartis — Decera's sequencing / treat-to-target IgAN program; layer Vertex's mechanism into a comparative framework rather than a solo-agent talk.

SUPPORTERS.name: Regeneron / Sanofi
SUPPORTERS.focus: Type-2 inflammation flagship (dupilumab) extending into eosinophilic esophagitis and allergy/derm.
SUPPORTERS.cost: EoE is newly a biologic-eligible disease. If GI/allergy clinicians aren't taught the Th2 pathophysiology and long-term care model, patients stay on PPIs/diet alone and biologic-eligible patients go unidentified.
SUPPORTERS.opp: CME Outfitters just launched EoE for them. Decera can differentiate with a GI↔allergy co-management EoE program (the two specialties rarely co-educate) linked to the broader type-2 story across AD, asthma and CRSwNP — an integrated curriculum competitors fragment.

SUPPORTERS.name: Astellas
SUPPORTERS.focus: Retina / complement — geographic atrophy in dry AMD.
SUPPORTERS.cost: GA is irreversible and progressive and the clinical debate is whether/when to treat given burden. Without a decision framework now, eligible patients progress to central vision loss before the treat/no-treat conversation happens.
SUPPORTERS.opp: ACHL's GA session is single-specialty. Decera's angle: a benefit–burden shared-decision GA program with patient-facing decision aids (injection frequency vs slowing progression) — decision science, not just trial data, in an ophthalmology lane where Decera has little competition.

SUPPORTERS.name: Genentech
SUPPORTERS.cost: Lupus nephritis outcomes hinge on early aggressive therapy; delayed education means continued renal damage before newer agents are used and a persistent rheumatology–nephrology coordination gap.
SUPPORTERS.opp: Decera can build the rheumatology↔nephrology LN co-management pathway (who leads, when to biopsy, how to escalate) — an interprofessional slot single-specialty SLE talks leave open.

SUPPORTERS.name: Insmed
SUPPORTERS.cost: A first-in-class approval window; if pulmonologists aren't taught to identify and phenotype bronchiectasis now, the eligible population stays under-recognized and the launch under-performs.
SUPPORTERS.opp: Almost no competitor education here (only Power-Pak). Decera can own bronchiectasis end-to-end — case-finding → phenotyping → new-mechanism positioning — an uncontested rare-pulmonary lane.

SUPPORTERS.name: Apellis Pharmaceuticals
SUPPORTERS.focus: Complement in rare kidney disease (C3 glomerulopathy).
SUPPORTERS.cost: Ultra-rare and newly treatable; without shared-decision education the tiny eligible population is missed entirely.
SUPPORTERS.opp: Decera can pair C3G with its IgAN/complement work into a complement-in-nephrology mini-curriculum — one immunology thread across rare kidney diseases, which no one bundles.

SUPPORTERS.name: HAE group (Intellia · Pharming · Pharvaris)
SUPPORTERS.focus: Hereditary angioedema — on-demand + prophylaxis + emerging gene editing.
SUPPORTERS.cost: HAE is diagnostically delayed by years; if allergy/PCP education lags, attacks are mismanaged and prophylaxis or gene-editing candidates are never identified.
SUPPORTERS.opp: RMEI owns the generic HAE talk. Decera's differentiated slot is an HAE long-term therapy-selection program (on-demand vs prophylaxis vs one-time gene editing — how to choose and counsel), a decision framework competitors don't offer.
